Financial Benefit: Bank loan of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore (covers both starting money and daily running money). Also get a Rupay debit card
Target Gender: Any (men must be SC/ST; women can apply regardless of caste
Target Community / Category: SC/ST and/or Women
Business Type / Industry: New (greenfield) business only — manufacturing, services, trading, or agriculture-related work
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can get this loan if: (1) you are starting a brand-new business, (2) you are 18 or older, (3) if you are a man, you must be from SC or ST community, (4) if you are a woman, any woman can apply, (5) you have never failed to repay a bank loan before, (6) if it's a company/partnership, SC/ST or woman must own more than half of it
Documents Required: ID proof (Voter ID/Passport/License/PAN); Address proof (electricity bill/phone bill/Voter ID); Business address proof; Letter saying you have no loan default; Company/partnership papers (if any); List of your assets and debts + income tax returns; Rent agreement (if renting shop); Pollution clearance (if needed); MSME registration (if you have one); 2-year money plan for the business; Property papers for anything offered as security; Caste certificate (if SC/ST); For loans above ₹25 lakh — extra business project report and details of machines, staff, and competitors
How to Apply: Apply at your nearest bank branch, OR contact your District's Lead District Manager (LDM), OR apply online at standupmitra.in — register with your business and personal details, then a bank will contact you to finish the loan process

Scheme Name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes
Financial Benefit: Money for your business — ₹10 lakh to ₹15 crore. Loan interest is 4% per year (3.75% for SC women and disabled entrepreneurs), or the government can invest in your business directly
Target Community / Category: Scheduled Caste (SC) only — not for ST, OBC, or General category
Business Type / Industry: Manufacturing, services, or tech/innovation businesses (including startups)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can get this if: (1) you are from the SC community, (2) your company has been running for at least 6 months (for smaller amounts) or 12 months (for larger amounts) with SC ownership of at least 51%, (3) for tech ideas, you must have a patent or support from a recognized incubator. Note: This is only for registered companies — not for solo proprietors or basic partnership firms applying directly
Documents Required: Caste certificate; A detailed project report about your business; Papers from your incubation center (for tech projects with incubator support); Patent/copyright papers (for tech projects without incubator support); Sanction letter (if government subsidy is involved
How to Apply: Register on the official website with your email and phone number (OTP verification), then log in and fill the application form, upload your documents, and submit. After that, a review team checks your papers, visits your business site, and a final committee approves the funding — money is then released in parts.

Scheme Name: Samriddhi – Scheme for SC/ST Students for Setting Start-Ups
Financial Benefit: ₹2 lakh seed money per startup (free money, no need to pay back) for 9 selected students per institute
Target Community / Category: Scheduled Caste (SC) / Scheduled Tribe (ST) students only
Business Type / Industry: Any new startup registered by the student
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Important: This scheme is not applied for directly by entrepreneurs. Your college/institute applies on your behalf. You can only benefit if: (1) you are SC or ST, (2) you are in your final year of degree/diploma, (3) you already have a registered company/startup in your name, (4) your institute is approved by AICTE and chosen to run this scheme, (5) you are not already getting money from another AICTE/government scheme for the same startup
Documents Required: For the student: Proof you're in final year; Proof your company/startup is registered in your name. (The institute handles all other paperwork — approval papers, bank details, faculty records, budget forms, etc
How to Apply: This is applied for by the Institute, not the student. The institute logs into the AICTE portal, fills in institute and bank details, adds a faculty coordinator, submits a project proposal, and validates the application. Students only need to register with a startup and their institute to be considered for one of the 9 selected slots

Scheme Name: Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission (ASIIM)
Financial Benefit: Up to ₹30 lakh over 3 years to build your idea (₹10 lakh/year) — pays for incubator costs, hardware, software, a monthly stipend, travel, patent filing, and workspace. If your startup does well, you can then get up to ₹15 crore more in funding
Target Community / Category: Scheduled Caste (SC) and SC Divyang (disabled) students only
Business Type / Industry: Innovative/tech startup ideas, especially ones solving social or economic problems
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can get this if: (1) you are SC or SC Divyang, (2) your idea has been picked by a recognized incubator (like a TBI, Atal Incubation Center, or similar), OR you won an award in Smart India Hackathon, OR your startup is backed by a company's CSR funds, (3) you agree to convert your firm into a Private/Public Limited company with at least 51% SC ownership before getting the money. Note: This does not cover businesses in RBI's restricted/negative sectors
Documents Required: Proof of SC or SC Divyang status; Company registration papers (Private/Public Limited); Shareholding document showing 51% SC ownership; Proof your incubator selected you; Proof of Smart India Hackathon award (if that's how you qualify); Your project proposal document
How to Apply: Register on the official website, log in, fill in the form, upload documents, and submit. After that, your incubator (TBI) recommends you, your idea gets auto-selected for incubation, you form your company, and funds are released yearly based on your progress

Scheme Name: Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan(PM VIKAS)
Financial Benefit: Free skill training (traditional + modern), stipend during training, free schooling support for class 8/10/12, and business/leadership training for women (with help getting loans and selling products)
Minimum Age: 14 years (18 for the women's leadership/business track)
Target Gender: Women get priority — 33% of skilling seats, 50% of education seats, and 100% of leadership/business seats are reserved for them; men can join skilling and education
Target Community / Category: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis (a small number of non-minority poor candidates also allowed)
Business Type / Industry: Any traditional craft or modern trade skill; also supports women starting their own business
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can join if: (1) you are 14–45 years old (18–45 for the women's business track), (2) you belong to one of the 6 minority communities — Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, or Parsi (a small number of non-minority low-income people can also join), (3) for the business track, you must be a woman, (4) you have the right education level for the course you're choosing. People with disabilities get extra reserved seats
Documents Required: Aadhaar card + Aadhaar-linked bank account; EWS (income) certificate — only if you are not from a minority community; Proof of your education level for the course you want
How to Apply: Go to the SIDH portal website, register and complete your e-KYC, set a password, verify your phone number, then search for PM VIKAS courses, pick up to 5 batches you're interested in, and wait for the training center to approve you. Confirm your seat

Financial Benefit: Free training, plus subsidy on your project cost — 44% subsidy for women, SC/ST, and candidates from NE/Hill states; 36% for everyone else. Project cost cap is ₹20 lakh solo (₹25 lakh for very good projects), or up to ₹1 crore for a group of 5+ people.
Target Location: All India (extra subsidy for NE and Hill state candidates)
Target Community / Category: Any — extra subsidy for SC/ST
Business Type / Industry: Agriculture and allied services — soil testing labs, veterinary services, seed/plant units, bee-keeping, fisheries, farm equipment repair, IT kiosks for farmers, rural marketing, and more
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can get this if: (1) you are 18–60 years old, (2) you have a degree, diploma, or 12th-level qualification in Agriculture or a related field (like Horticulture, Fisheries, Veterinary Science, Dairy, etc.), (3) you are willing to complete free training before starting. Note: Retired people getting a pension can still train and start a self-funded project, but can't get the subsidy
Documents Required: Aadhaar number; Email ID; Latest education certificate; Bank account details; Your photo. (If you don't have Aadhaar yet: Aadhaar enrolment slip + one of Voter ID/PAN/Passport/Ration Card/Bank Passbook/Driving License,etc)
How to Apply: Apply through the Jansamarth portal — visit the website, fill in the form, upload your documents, and submit. You can track your status later using your Applicant ID, mobile number, or Aadhaar number.

Financial Benefit: New unit: Government subsidy is 15% (Urban) / 25% (Rural) for General category and 25% (Urban) / 35% (Rural) for Special categories. Own contribution is 10% for General and 5% for Special categories. Maximum project cost for subsidy: ₹50 lakh for Manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for Business/Service. 2nd loan for existing units: 15% subsidy, or 20% in NER and Hill States, subject to limits.
Target Community / Category: General; SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, Ex-Servicemen, Transgenders, Differently Abled, NER, Aspirational Districts, Hill and Border Areas
Business Type / Industry: New micro-enterprises in manufacturing, business and services; eligible existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units for upgradation
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Any individual aged 18 or above can apply for a new unit. There is no income limit. For projects above ₹10 lakh in Manufacturing or ₹5 lakh in Business/Service, the applicant must have passed at least Class 8. The project must be new and must not have already received government subsidy. Only one person from a family (self and spouse) can get assistance for a new project. Existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units can apply for a 2nd loan if the first loan was repaid, the subsidy lock-in was completed, and the unit is profitable with growth potential.
Documents Required: Caste Certificate; Special Category Certificate if applicable; Rural Area Certificate; Project Report; Education/EDP/Skill Development Training Certificate; other applicable documents
How to Apply: Apply online through the PMEGP portal. Select “Application For New Unit” or “Application For Existing Units (2nd Loan)”, fill the form, upload documents and submit. Registered applicants can log in to track/apply for the second-loan subsidy.

Scheme Name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme
Financial Benefit: Reimbursement of 80% of the EPC membership fee, up to ₹20,000 per financial year, whichever is lower. GST and other taxes are not included.
Target Community / Category: SC/ST
Business Type / Industry: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: The applicant must belong to SC or ST category and represent a Micro or Small Enterprise. The enterprise must have the required Udyam Registration and valid Import Export Code (IEC). For partnership/LLP/private companies, SC/ST ownership must meet the required shareholding condition. The scheme helps pay part of the membership fee charged by an Export Promotion Council.
Documents Required: Udyam Registration; GST number if applicable; PAN; SC/ST caste certificate; shareholding details; partnership deed/MOA/AOA where applicable; valid IEC; valid RCMC from the Export Promotion Council; previous RCMC for renewal if applicable; proof of previous reimbursement if applicable; EPC membership fee receipt and GST invoice; cancelled cheque of enterprise current account
How to Apply: Apply online through the National SC-ST Hub portal. Register with name, email and mobile number, create a password, log in, fill in the required details and submit the application with documents.

Financial Benefit: Duty-free import of eligible inputs used to make export products. Exemption can include Basic Customs Duty, Additional Customs Duty, Education Cess, Anti-dumping Duty, Safeguard Duty, IGST and Compensation Cess, wherever applicable and subject to scheme conditions.
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: Manufacturer exporters and merchant exporters tied to supporting manufacturers
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: The applicant must be a manufacturer exporter or a merchant exporter linked to a supporting manufacturer. The imported inputs must be used to make the exported product. The exporter must meet the required input norms and achieve at least 15% value addition. Export obligation normally must be completed within 18 months from the date of Authorisation, or within the period notified by DGFT.
Documents Required: IEC copy; export product description; export ITC-HS code; export quantity and FOB value; import item description; import ITC-HS code; import quantity and CIF value; IGST and customs duty details; port of registration; valid RCMC; industrial licence where applicable; CA certificate; CA certificate of consumption for last 3 yea
How to Apply: Apply online through the DGFT portal. Get/update IEC, register DSC, obtain RCMC, then go to Services → Advance Authorisation / DFIA → Apply for Advance Authorisation (ANF 4A), fill in the details, upload documents and submit.

Scheme Name: Incredible India Bed and Breakfast establishment
Financial Benefit: No money given. You get an official "Silver" or "Gold" star rating, free publicity, and your name in the government's tourist directory.
Target Location: States/UTs with no own B&B approval scheme
Target Community / Category: All communities
Business Type / Industry: Bed & Breakfast / Homestay accommodation
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You own a small guest house with 1 to 6 rooms (max 12 beds). You do not live there yourself — you must hire a caretaker who lives on site and looks after guests. You serve breakfast and show your prices clearly to guests before they book.
Documents Required: GST number, PAN number, FSSAI license (if you serve food), other papers if asked
How to Apply: 1. Go to the NIDHI portal online. 2. Pick Silver or Gold. 3. Fill the form online. 4. Upload your papers. 5. Pay the fee online (card/UPI only, no cash). 6. Submit. 7. To renew later, apply again on the same site and pay again.

Financial Benefit: Monthly help: up to ₹20,000 a month for buying stock and keeping medicines ready. Extra one-time help: ₹2 lakh for women, SC/ST, disabled persons, ex-servicemen, and people in certain far or hilly areas (₹1.5 lakh for furniture, ₹0.5 lakh for computer/printer/internet). You also earn a 20% margin on every medicine sold
Target Location: India, with special focus on hilly, island, North-Eastern, and "aspirational" (less developed) districts
Target Community / Category: General public; extra benefit for women, SC/ST, disabled (Divyangjan), and ex-servicemen
Business Type / Industry: Medicine shop (Janaushadhi Kendra / generic medicine store)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must have a Pharmacy degree (D.Pharma or B.Pharma), OR hire a qualified pharmacist to run the shop. NGOs and trusts can also apply if they employ a pharmacist. Government hospitals prefer trusts/NGOs but individuals can apply too.
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Pharmacist registration certificate, Darpan ID (NGOs only), Registration Certificate (for NGOs/trusts), SC/ST or Disability certificate (if applying for extra money), last 2 years income tax returns (private entities), last 6 months bank statement, rental/space agreement, drug license, 3 cheques + 1 cancelled cheque from an Indian nationalized bank
How to Apply: 1. Go to the official website. 2. Fill in the form and pick your category (woman, SC, ST, disabled, etc.) — this cannot be changed later. 3. Pay ₹5,000 fee online (free if you are in a special category, with proof). 4. If approved, sign the agreement. 5. Get your drug license in the shop's name, set up the billing software, and give the required bank cheques before your medicines arrive.

Financial Benefit: Government pays 40% of project cost (up to ₹10 lakh) as a subsidy. You pay only 5% yourself. The bank gives a loan for the remaining 55%. Extra loan (up to 25% more) is available for running costs, but that part gets no subsidy.
Target Location: India, extra focus on North Eastern Region
Target Community / Category: General public; special focus on SC/ST and North East communities
Business Type / Industry: Coir business (making coir fibre, yarn, rope, or coir products)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be an 18+ Indian citizen. There is no income limit. You must start a new coir-making unit (fibre, yarn, or products). You can apply alone, or as a company, self-help group, NGO, trust, or society. You must not have already gotten a similar government subsidy for the same purpose. Only one person per family (self or spouse) can get this help.
Documents Required: Filled application form, land/property title deed, proof of coir industry experience, proof of Coir Board training, machinery invoice, Industrial Establishment Certificate from District Industries Centre, workshed construction plan certified by an engineer, project profile, Caste Certificate (if SC/ST)
How to Apply: 1. Fill the application form. 2. Submit it at your nearest Coir Board office. 3. Attend a required 5-day training program. 4. Your application is checked and sent to a selection committee. 5. If approved, it goes to the bank. 6. Once the bank approves, pay your 5% share within 30 days. 7. Coir Board sends the subsidy to the bank. 8. Bank gives you the loan within 30 days. 9. Finish setting up your unit within 6 months. 10. Officials visit and check your unit before final subsidy is settled

Financial Benefit: Loan up to ₹1.25 lakh (up to 90% of your business cost, max unit cost ₹1,40,000). You pay only 2.5% interest to NSFDC, but the local bank/agency may charge you up to 6.5%. Pay back over 3 years, with a 3-month break before payments start.
Target Community / Category: Scheduled Caste (SC) only
Business Type / Industry: Small trade/business (e.g. betel leaf shop, bakery, candle making, cycle repair, goat rearing, beauty parlour, vegetable vending, incense stick making, fish vending, milch animal rearing, papad making, pickle making, tea shop, and similar work)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must belong to a Scheduled Caste. Your family's yearly income must be below ₹3,00,000 (rural or urban). Groups like partnership firms or co-operative societies can also apply, but every single member must be SC and earn below ₹3,00,000 a year.
Documents Required: Passport-size photo, Aadhaar Card, Income certificate, Caste certificate, Residence proof, Bank passbook/bank details, other documents if asked
How to Apply: 1. Go to your District Office of the State Channelizing Agency (SCA), or a bank/NBFC partnered with NSFDC. 2. Submit the application form with your caste, income, and business details. 3. The District Office checks your papers. 4. It is sent to the Head Office. 5. The Head Office checks if your business plan is workable and sends it to NSFDC. 6. NSFDC reviews it and approves it if in order. 7. Money is sent to the bank/agency. 8. The bank/agency gives you the loan. 9. You repay the loan as per the schedule given to you. Note: You cannot contact NSFDC directly — you must go through your local SCA/bank.

Financial Benefit: Government pays back part of your machine/building cost (30% in some areas, 50% in others). Government also pays part of your loan interest (3% or 5% off, for 7 years). Government also gives back all the GST you pay, for up to 10 years.
Target Location: Only the 8 North-Eastern states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura
Target Community / Category: All communities
Business Type / Industry: Factory/manufacturing business or service business (new or expanding). This is for larger businesses — you need to invest at least ₹1 crore in machinery, not for very small shops.
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must set up a new factory or service business, or expand an existing one, in the North-East. You need proper business registration, a signed land lease/ownership paper, GST registration, and project reports showing your plan is workable.
Documents Required: Detailed Project Report (DPR), land ownership/lease papers, bank appraisal report, incorporation/firm registration certificate, PAN card, GST certificate, Udyam (MSME) registration certificate
How to Apply: 1. Go to the official UNNATI website. 2. Sign up using your email or phone number. 3. Log in and fill the online form with your business details. 4. Upload all required documents (DPR, land papers, bank report, etc.). 5. Check everything and submit online.

Financial Benefit: You get a monthly stipend while training (₹5,000 to ₹9,000, depending on your schooling level). Government pays 25% of this (up to ₹1,500/month) directly into your bank account; the company pays the rest.
Minimum Age: 14 years (18 years for risky/hazardous trades); must be 35 or younger when you register
Target Location: All India, with extra focus on North-East and less developed ("aspirational") districts
Target Community / Category: General public; especially those who did short skill-training courses (like DDUGKY, PMKVY, NULM)
Business Type / Industry: Not a business — this is for individuals to get on-the-job apprenticeship training and become skilled workers
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be between 14 and 35 years old (18+ for hazardous trades). You need an Aadhaar card with completed e-KYC on the portal. Training lasts 6 months to 2 years depending on the trade. Anyone, including those who did short skill courses before, can apply.
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card, other documents depending on the trade you choose
How to Apply: 1. Go to the official Apprenticeship India website. 2. Click Login/Register and choose "Candidate." 3. Enter your mobile number and email to register. 4. Enter your Aadhaar number and complete e-KYC — this is required to finish registration. 5. Verify using mobile OTP.

Scheme Name: Export Oriented Production: Large Cardamom Certified Nursery (Unit)
Financial Benefit: Money is given per seedling grown, paid straight to your bank account after the plants are ready: General category gets ₹3 per seedling (about 1/3rd of the cost). SC/ST farmers get ₹6.75 per seedling (about 3/4th of the cost).
Target Location: Sikkim, Darjeeling & Kalimpong (West Bengal), and other North-Eastern states
Target Community / Category: General public; higher payment for SC/ST
Business Type / Industry: Farming — growing a large cardamom plant nursery
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be a farmer or farmer group with land and water for a nursery. You must be able to grow at least 1,000 seedlings (up to 5,000). Officials will visit your nursery to guide and check your work. Farmer groups must be a registered group (Society/FPC/FPO/SHG).
Documents Required: Land ownership/possession paper (Parcha copy), Aadhaar card, SC/ST certificate (if applicable), Bank passbook copy, No Objection Certificate from panchayat (if land is not in your name)
How to Apply: 1. Submit your application with documents to your nearest Spices Board office. 2. Submit extra documents if the officer asks (like SC/ST certificate). 3. If applying as a group, register as a legal group and sign an agreement with the Board on ₹200 stamp paper. 4. An officer inspects your nursery and gives a permit. 5. After the work is finished, a final inspection is done, and approved cases are recommended for payment (first-come-first-served).

Financial Benefit: Government pays up to 50% of your setup cost, up to ₹1 lakh per seat/workstation. Extra money if you hire mostly women (+7.5%), hire disabled workers (+2%), create more jobs than promised (+10%), or are a local entrepreneur (+5%).
Target Location: North-Eastern states only: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura
Target Community / Category: General public; extra incentive for local entrepreneurs and disabled workers
Business Type / Industry: Large company setting up a call center / IT services (BPO/ITeS) office — this is for registered companies, not individuals or small shops
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: This is only for registered companies (Pvt Ltd, LLP, etc.), not individual people. You need at least 25 seats/workstations, a large office space, past yearly earnings of at least ₹1 crore, and the ability to run the business for at least 3 years. This is a large-business scheme, not for micro or small entrepreneurs.
Documents Required: Company registration certificate, PAN, GST certificate, Labour Dept. registration (if applicable), tax registration, tender documents & fee proof, seat/location details, bank account details, company contact details
How to Apply: 1. Go to the official STPI website. 2. Read the scheme guidelines. 3. Submit your proposal/bid online. 4. Upload required documents; your proposal is reviewed. 5. If approved, set up your BPO/ITeS office. 6. Submit reports and claims online to get your payment.

Financial Benefit: Money to help travel/hotel businesses promote themselves in other countries: 90% of flight tickets, 90% of stall/exhibition costs, and up to 5 nights of hotel stay (max ₹10,000/night) — total up to ₹3,50,000 per trip. Separately, up to ₹1,00,000/year for online marketing (50% of the cost).
Target Location: All India (business location); promotion happens overseas
Target Community / Category: General public (business owners)
Business Type / Industry: Travel & tourism business — travel agent, tour operator, hotel, bed & breakfast, homestay, motel, guest house, restaurant, or similar tourism-related business
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Your business must already be officially approved by the Ministry of Tourism or your State/UT Tourism Department. Your business must have earned at least ₹1 crore to ₹2 crore in recent years to get up to 2 trips a year of support, or ₹2 crore+ to get up to 3 trips a year.
Documents Required: Proof of tourism business approval, a signed declaration that you are not under investigation/banned, an income certificate signed by a Chartered Accountant (for approval); for getting your money back: past 3 years' financial details, flight tickets/boarding passes, a short trip report (250 words max), and original bills/receipts for everything
How to Apply: 1. Before your trip, get approval from the Ministry of Tourism (apply at least 21 days early). 2. Fill the approval form and attach documents; email it to mda-tourism@gov.in. 3. After your trip, fill the claim form and attach your bills, tickets, and trip report. 4. Email the claim within 45 days of finishing the trip. Note: applications are only accepted by email, not on paper.

Financial Benefit: No money. You get a trophy and certificate only.
Target Location: All India, plus Indian Embassies abroad
Target Community / Category: Not applicable (this is for government bodies, not individuals)
Business Type / Industry: Not applicable — this is not a scheme for individuals or small businesses. It is an award for States/UTs, Districts, Indian Missions Abroad, e-commerce platforms, and Central Ministries for their work promoting local products.
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: This award is only for government offices and official bodies — not for individual shop owners, artisans, or entrepreneurs. Only entities that did work promoting an official ODOP (One District One Product) can apply.
Documents Required: Proof that you are an official State/UT, District, Mission, e-commerce platform, or Ministry, proof of promotion work done, and reports showing results
How to Apply: 1. Go to the official website and register. 2. Choose "Individual" or "Organization" as the nominator type. 3. Fill in your details (name, Aadhaar, contact info, etc.). 4. Log in, select the award category, and click "Nominate/Apply Now." 5. Fill the online form and submit.

Financial Benefit: Citation and memento; Travel Allowance and Dearness Allowance for attending the award function. Previous editions awarded ₹3 lakh to winners and ₹1 lakh to runners-up.
Target Community / Category: Indian citizens, institutions, industries, organisations, startups and government-created entities
Business Type / Industry: Petrochemicals, polymers, research, innovation, manufacturing, startups and related fields
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Applicant must be an Indian citizen or an eligible institution, industry, organisation or startup registered in India. The innovation must be an original product/process or improvement, provide useful benefits, and be no more than 3 years old. Idea-only or theoretical innovations are not eligible. Teams can have up to 5 members. Previous winners of the last 3 editions are not eligible.
Documents Required: Innovation highlights; detailed technical description with photos; principle and originality/novelty details; advantages over alternatives; publication/patent details; test report; user/field trial report; commercialization/collaboration details; self-appraisal; previous award details; business/collaboration details with government bodies/PSUs; 3-year action plan; signed undertaking certificate with seal; Aadhaar Card
How to Apply: Apply online through the official portal. Choose the suitable category/form for Individual, Team, Industry, Academic Institution, R&D Institution or MSME. Fill in details, upload the innovation documents and technical reports, accept the undertaking and submit for screening and evaluation.

Financial Benefit: Government guarantee covers 85% of loan/credit up to ₹10 crore and 75% for credit up to ₹20 crore. This helps eligible startups get loans without collateral.
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: Startups using venture debt, working capital, debentures, or other eligible debt facilities
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must be a DPIIT-recognised startup. The startup must not be in loan default or classified as an NPA. An eligible bank, NBFC, financial institution or SEBI-registered AIF must certify the startup and provide the eligible credit facility.
Documents Required: DPIIT Startup Recognition Certificate, PAN, company registration documents, financial statements, loan/credit documents, KYC documents, bank details and other documents asked by the lender
How to Apply: Apply to an eligible bank, NBFC, financial institution or SEBI-registered AIF for an eligible loan. The Member Institution applies for the CGSS guarantee cover.

Scheme Name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 – Special Projects
Financial Benefit: Free skill training. Training cost is paid by the scheme. Up to ₹500 for uniform/kit. Free assessment and re-assessment. ₹5,000 support for assistive devices for PwD candidates. Boarding, lodging and travel support may be given to women, PwD and candidates from special areas. 1-year accidental insurance and free digital certificate are also provided.
Target Location: India; special focus on remote, hilly, border, tribal and LWE-affected areas
Target Community / Category: Marginalised and vulnerable groups, SC, ST, women, PwD and other groups needing special support
Business Type / Industry: Skill training, future-skill jobs, upskilling and reskilling
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Applicant must be an Indian citizen aged 15–45 years and have a valid Aadhaar. The applicant must meet the requirements of the chosen job course and belong to a marginalised/vulnerable group or another group needing special attention, or choose a future-skill job role. The person must not repeat the same job role already completed
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card; other documents may be required depending on the selected job role/course
How to Apply: Register on the Skill India Digital website/app using mobile OTP/eKYC. Complete the profile, choose a course and nearby training centre, enrol, complete training and On-the-Job Training, then take the assessment.

Scheme Name: Group Workshed Scheme for Shuttleless Looms
Financial Benefit: Construction subsidy: 40% for General category (up to ₹400/sq.ft), 75% for SC (up to ₹750/sq.ft), and 90% for ST (up to ₹900/sq.ft). Maximum area: 400 sq.ft per shuttleless loom, 40% of loomage area for weaving preparation, and 125 sq.ft per dormitory person.
Target Community / Category: General, SC, ST powerloom weavers/entrepreneurs
Business Type / Industry: Powerloom and shuttleless loom weaving
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: A group must have at least 4 weavers/entrepreneurs with separate legal entities. The group must have at least 24 shuttleless looms up to 230 cm wide, or 16 looms wider than 230 cm. Each beneficiary must have at least 4 looms. Only TUFS-compatible machines can be used. Eligible applicants include State Government/agencies, registered cooperative societies, companies/LLPs formed by powerloom owners, and local powerloom associations.
Documents Required: Beneficiary/group registration documents, legal entity documents, details of looms and machinery, project/construction details, and any documents or information requested by the Textile Commissioner
How to Apply: Offline. Scheme advertisements are published in newspapers. Eligible groups can follow the application instructions given in the advertisement and submit the required documents.

Scheme Name: Scheme for Reimbursement of Testing and Certification Charges for Start-ups and Telecom MSEs
Financial Benefit: Start-ups: up to 75% of testing and certification charges; Micro Enterprises: up to 60%; Small Enterprises: up to 50%. Maximum reimbursement is ₹50 lakh per applicant during the scheme period.
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: Telecom and ICT products/equipment
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Applicant must be a DPIIT-registered Start-up or MSME-registered Micro/Small Enterprise incorporated in India. Annual revenue must not be more than ₹5 crore in any financial year. A Start-up must not have raised more than ₹10 crore. Testing/certification must be for telecom equipment under MTCTE or voluntary certification. The same testing cost must not have already received government reimbursement.
Documents Required: Certificate of Incorporation; audited financial statements; DPIIT Registration or Udyam Registration Certificate; lab TEC/NCCS designation or NABL accreditation certificate; test reports and product certificate; testing lab invoice/receipt; certification fee payment receipt; undertaking for revenue/funding limits; bank details and cancelled cheque; self-declaration of no duplicate government reimbursement; PAN card; other required documents
How to Apply: Apply online through the TEC portal before the quarterly deadline. Upload the required documents. The application is checked and evaluated before approval. After approval, the reimbursement is paid to the applicant.

Scheme Name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for IT Hardware
Financial Benefit: Incentive of 4% to 2% / 1% on net additional sales of eligible IT hardware made in India. Benefit is available for 4 years.
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: IT hardware manufacturing companies; Global Companies and Domestic Companies
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must be a company registered in India and making eligible IT hardware such as laptops, tablets, All-in-One PCs or servers. The company must meet the required investment, production and sales targets and follow the scheme rules. This scheme is not for individual people or ordinary shops.
Documents Required: Certificate of Incorporation; company registration documents; audited financial statements; investment proof; production and sales data; bank account details; statutory approvals and licences; undertaking/declaration; other documents required by PMA
How to Apply: Apply online at the PLI IT Hardware portal. Register the company, fill the application, upload documents and submit it. After approval, make eligible products in India and submit yearly incentive claims.

Financial Benefit: Gold Award: ₹10 lakh to the organization, trophy and certificate. Silver Award: ₹5 lakh to the organization, trophy and certificate. Certificates for up to 4 team members.
Target Community / Category: All eligible organizations
Business Type / Industry: Government departments, local bodies, academic institutions, research organizations and DPIIT-defined startups with e-Governance projects
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: The applicant can be a Central/State/UT Government department, district, urban local body, academic institution, research organization or eligible startup. It must have an e-Governance project using technology. The project must have started between 01.10.2023 and 30.09.2025 and be fully working on 01.12.2025. The project should improve innovation, efficiency, transparency or citizen services. Only one project can be submitted in one category.
Documents Required: Project proposal with details; self-certification form; proof that the project was implemented and is working; organization registration details and email; team member details (up to 3 members plus project head); documents showing project impact and results; presentation materials if shortlisted
How to Apply: Apply online on the National e-Governance portal. Register the organization, log in, select an award category, fill the project details, upload documents and submit before the deadline. Shortlisted applicants may need to present the project to the jury

Scheme Name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)
Financial Benefit: Incentive based on additional sales of eligible food products. Rates vary by product and year: 10% to 8% for Ready-to-Cook/Ready-to-Eat and Processed Fruits & Vegetables, 6% to 4% for Marine Products (up to 10% for value-added marine products), and 10% to 4% for Mozzarella Cheese. For foreign branding and marketing, 50% of eligible spending is supported, up to 3% of food-product sales or ₹50 crore per year, whichever is lower.
Target Community / Category: All eligible food businesses; special category for SMEs making innovative/organic products
Business Type / Industry: Food manufacturing: Ready-to-Cook/Ready-to-Eat foods, millet-based foods, processed fruits and vegetables, marine products, mozzarella cheese, and innovative/organic food products; also branding and marketing abroad
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must manufacture eligible food products in India and sell them. Applicant must meet the required minimum sales and investment for its category. The required manufacturing chain must take place in India, except for additives, flavours and edible oils. Applicant must not be bankrupt, a wilful defaulter, fraud-reported by a financial institution, or on the SEBI debarred list. Large companies, eligible SMEs and applicants doing foreign branding/marketing can apply under the relevant category.
Documents Required: Application form; audit undertaking; manufacturing-site details; shareholding details; company registration/MOA/partnership deed; annual financial statements and reports; eligible food-product sales data; investment proof; Chartered Accountant certificate for sales; Chartered Engineer certificate for investment where applicable; 3% performance bank guarantee after approval; other documents required in the EOI
How to Apply: Apply online when MoFPI releases an Expression of Interest (EOI). Visit the PLISFPI portal, fill the application, provide manufacturing and financial details, upload documents, pay the application fee and submit. After selection, submit the required 3% performance bank guarantee

Scheme Name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Millet-Based Products (PLISMBP)
Financial Benefit: Incentive of 10% on eligible additional sales in initial years, reducing to 8% in later years. Maximum total incentive: ₹100 crore for Large Entities and ₹40 crore for MSMEs during the scheme period.
Target Community / Category: All eligible food businesses
Business Type / Industry: Manufacturing of packaged and branded Ready-to-Cook (RTC) / Ready-to-Eat (RTE) millet-based food products
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must be a business making or planning to make eligible millet food products in India. Products must contain more than 15% millet. Business must meet the minimum sales requirement and achieve at least 10% yearly sales growth (CAGR). MSMEs must have Udyam Registration. The manufacturing process must mainly take place in India. Applicant/promoters must not be bankrupt, wilful defaulters, or on the relevant CIBIL/SEBI debarred lists.
Documents Required: Application Form; company/partnership registration documents; shareholding/partner details; last 3 years audited financial statements; PBT/PAT details; PAN; GST Registration Certificate; Udyam Registration Certificate for MSMEs; FSSAI License; auditor/CA certificate for sales; domestic and export sales details; product details and millet-content declaration; product photographs showing millet content; Credit History/Commercial CIBIL Report; integrity undertaking; audit consent; manufacturing facility details; promoter/director/key-person details with PAN/DIN; external credit rating if available
How to Apply: Apply online when MoFPI releases an Expression of Interest (EOI). Register on the PMA portal, fill the application, upload documents, provide manufacturing-site details, give audit consent, pay the application fee (₹1 lakh for Large Entities or ₹10,000 for MSMEs) and submit before the deadline. Selected applicants submit yearly incentive claims.

Scheme Name: International cooperative scheme-Capacity Building of First Time MSE Exporters
Financial Benefit: RCMC: 75% of cost, up to ₹20,000. Export insurance: up to ₹10,000 per financial year. Testing and quality certification: 75% of cost, up to ₹1 lakh per MSE per financial year, for maximum 3 certificates
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), first-time exporters
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must be a Micro or Small Enterprise with valid Udyam Registration. The Importer Exporter Code (IEC) must be less than 3 years old on the date of export shipment. The scheme helps first-time exporters pay part of the cost of RCMC, export insurance, and testing/quality certification
Documents Required: Udyam Registration; IEC Code; RCMC fee receipt; export proof; insurance premium receipt; testing/quality certificate; proof of export; proof that testing/certification is required for export; self-declaration that the same benefit was not taken under MAI; other prescribed claim documents
How to Apply: Apply online through the International Cooperation Scheme portal. Register as a new user or log in, submit the application/claim with required documents and expenditure details. RCMC, insurance and testing-certification claims follow the respective prescribed process through EPCs, ECGC or NSIC.

Financial Benefit: Government pays 75% of project cost for Micro Enterprises and 60% for Small & Medium Enterprises, up to ₹40 lakh. For approved student projects, government pays 75% of project cost, up to ₹2.5 lakh.
Target Community / Category: All
Business Type / Industry: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: The business must be a registered Micro, Small or Medium Enterprise. It must have a valid Udyam Registration or Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM). The scheme helps businesses develop new products, improve existing products and get advice from professional designers.
Documents Required: Udyam Registration/Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) certificate; registered mobile number
How to Apply: Apply online. Visit the MSME Innovative portal, select “Design”, click “Join Design Scheme”, enter the Udyam Registration Number and registered mobile number, validate and complete the application.

Financial Benefit: Govt gives 15%–35% of the business cost as a gift (you don't repay this part). Bank gives the rest as a loan. You pay only 5%–10% from your pocket. New business: up to ₹50 lakh (factory-type) or ₹20 lakh (shop/service-type).
Target Gender: All (women count as special category, get more subsidy)
Target Location: Works in both village and city areas
Target Community / Category: General public; more subsidy for SC/ST/OBC/Minority/Women/Ex-Army/Transgender/Disabled/NE Region/Hill & Border/Disaster-hit areas
Business Type / Industry: New factory-type (manufacturing) business or new shop/service business (must be NEW, not an old business)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you are 18 or older, want to start a brand-new business (not expand an old one), and have never taken money from a similar govt scheme before. Only one person per family can apply. If your business costs more than ₹10 lakh (factory-type) or ₹5 lakh (shop/service), you must have passed Class 8 in school. You cannot apply for: meat, tobacco, liquor, or paan/cigarette businesses, or farming/tea/coffee/rubber growing businesses.
Documents Required: Caste certificate, Special category certificate (if needed), Rural area certificate (if needed), Project report, Education/skill training certificate, ID proof
How to Apply: Apply online on the myScheme/PMEGP website: fill the form, upload documents, submit. Or apply offline: fill the paper form and hand it to your local KVIC/KVIB/DIC/Coir Board office, they will give you a receipt slip.

Scheme Name: Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME): Assistance for Reimbursement of CGTMSE Fees
Financial Benefit: Govt pays back 100% of the yearly bank fee you pay for your collateral-free loan (up to ₹2 crore loan), for 5 years. You don't pay this fee yourself.
Target Community / Category: General public (no caste/community restriction mentioned)
Business Type / Industry: Manufacturing businesses only (not for shop/service/trading businesses)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: your business is Micro/Small/Medium, you already took a collateral-free loan (called CGTMSE loan) from a bank, and you apply within 1 year of getting the loan money or before you start production (whichever is later). Shop, service, and trading businesses cannot apply.
Documents Required: Loan sanction letter copy, bank loan statement, Udyam registration copy, PAN card copy, business proof documents, ITR copy, project report, property documents, and other business papers (full list is long — ask your bank/DIC office for the checklist)
How to Apply: Apply online on the Investor Facilitation Portal (IFP): register with your email, verify it, log in, and fill in your business details and documents.

Financial Benefit: Loan up to ₹2,00,000 at only 5% yearly interest for starting your own work. If your business costs ₹2,00,000 or less, you don't need to put in any of your own money.
Target Location: All India (apply at your nearest SCA office)
Target Community / Category: Backward Classes (OBC) women
Business Type / Industry: Any self-employment / small business
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you are a woman between 18–55 years old, belong to a Backward Class, run or want to run your own small business, and your family's total yearly income is less than ₹3 lakh.
Documents Required: Aadhaar card, Ration card, Domicile certificate, Caste certificate (if reserved category), Passport-size photo
How to Apply: Go to your nearest SCA (State Channelising Agency) office, fill the application form by hand, write down your business idea and any training needed, and submit the form with your documents. Office finder: https://nsfdc.nic.in/channel-patrners/scas

Financial Benefit: Loan up to ₹1,40,000 at low interest to start your own work. Pay back over 3.5 years in small quarterly parts. Free training + stipend given if you join a women's group (SHG).
Target Location: All India (apply through State Channelising Agency offices)
Target Community / Category: SC/ST/OBC and other backward/minority women; groups of ~20 women (SHGs) preferred
Business Type / Industry: Any small business / income-generating work
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you are a woman between 18–55 years old, belong to SC/ST/OBC or a low-income family, your family's yearly income is less than ₹3 lakh, and you want to start your own work or join a women's group (SHG) for training and loan.
Documents Required: Address proof, ID proof, Aadhaar card, SHG membership ID (if in a group), Caste certificate (if applicable), Income certificate, Bank account details, Passport-size photo
How to Apply: Get the application form from the NSFDC website or your state government office, fill it with your details, attach documents, and submit it to your nearest SCA (State Channelising Agency) office.

Financial Benefit: Put money in (₹1,000 to ₹2,00,000) and get 7.5% yearly interest, added every 3 months. Get your money back after 2 years. You can also take out up to 40% of your money after 1 year if needed.
Minimum Age: No minimum age (can be opened for a girl child too, by a guardian)
Target Location: All India (Post Offices and select banks)
Target Community / Category: Open to all women — no caste/community restriction
Business Type / Industry: Not a business scheme — this is a savings/deposit scheme
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Any woman or girl (Indian citizen) can open this. A guardian can open it for a girl child. Only one account per person type, and only ₹2,00,000 total can be deposited across accounts.
Documents Required: Passport-size photo, Birth certificate (age proof), Aadhaar card, PAN card, Deposit slip/cheque, One ID+address proof (Passport, Driving licence, Voter ID, etc.)
How to Apply: Go to your nearest Post Office or listed bank, get/download the form, fill it, attach documents, deposit your money, and collect your certificate.

Scheme Name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme - Young Faculty Research Fellowship (YFRF)
Financial Benefit: ₹20,000 per month extra (on top of salary) + ₹5,00,000 per year for research costs, for up to 5 years
Minimum Age: Not specified (upper age limit is 40 years)
Target Location: All India (must work at a recognised institution)
Target Community / Category: General public — for PhD faculty/teachers only, no caste/community criteria
Business Type / Industry: Not a business scheme — this is for teachers/researchers doing PhD-level research, not for starting a business
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you are an Indian citizen, have a PhD with good grades, hold a permanent teaching/research job, are under 40 years old, and have not already taken this fellowship before. Your college must apply for you — you cannot apply on your own.
Documents Required: No fixed list — your institution collects the documents needed and applies on your behalf
How to Apply: Your institution applies for you online, when MeitY announces a "call for nominations." Each institution can only send up to 3 names per round.

Financial Benefit: Free hot cooked meal every school day (meets daily calorie and protein needs)
Minimum Age: Not specified (school-going age, Class 1 to 8, plus pre-school/Bal Vatika)
Target Community / Category: Open to all — no caste/community restriction
Business Type / Industry: Not a business scheme — this is a school meal benefit
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Any child studying in Class 1 to 8 (or pre-school) in a Government or Government-aided school gets this automatically. No application needed.
Documents Required: None required
How to Apply: No application needed — the meal is given automatically to all eligible children at school.

Scheme Name: Export Promotion Council Membership Reimbursement Scheme for SC/ST
Financial Benefit: Get back 80% of your membership fee (up to ₹20,000 per year) that you paid to join an Export Promotion Council
Target Community / Category: SC/ST community only (business owner must be SC/ST)
Business Type / Industry: Micro or Small business that exports goods (must already be a member of an Export Promotion Council)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you belong to SC or ST community, own or run a Micro/Small business, and have already paid membership fees to an Export Promotion Council. If it's a partnership/company, SC/ST owners must hold more than 51% share.
Documents Required: Udyam registration, GST number (if any), PAN card, Caste certificate, Partnership/company documents (if applicable), Import-Export Code (IEC) certificate, EPC membership certificate, Fee payment receipt & GST invoice, Cancelled cheque of business bank account
How to Apply: Go to the National SC-ST Hub website, sign up with your name/email/phone, create a password, log in, fill in your details, and submit the form online.

Scheme Name: Credit Based Schemes for SC - Term Loan (TL)
Financial Benefit: Loan up to ₹50,00,000 for your business (bank/NSFDC gives up to 95%, you pay only 2%–5%). Low interest: 6%–9% per year depending on loan size. If you are very poor (below poverty line), you may also get ₹10,000 or 50% of business cost as a free subsidy.
Target Location: All India (apply through your nearest Channelising Agency)
Target Community / Category: Scheduled Caste (SC) community only
Business Type / Industry: Any income-generating business (must be a workable/viable project)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you belong to the SC community, have a workable business idea, and your family's yearly income is less than ₹3 lakh. Your project plan will be checked by the local agency before the loan is approved.
Documents Required: Aadhaar card, Income certificate, Caste certificate, Bank account statement
How to Apply: Contact your nearest Channelising Agency (SCA/bank), fill the term loan form, submit your business plan and documents. Office finder: https://nsfdc.nic.in/channel-patrners/

Financial Benefit: Get back 80% of your product testing fee (up to ₹1,00,000), for testing your raw material, half-made goods, or finished products. Can be claimed many times in a year.
Target Community / Category: SC/ST community only (business owner must be SC/ST)
Business Type / Industry: Micro or Small business (must be registered on Udyam portal)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: you belong to SC or ST community, own a Micro/Small business registered on Udyam, and have paid to test your products at a government-approved lab (NABL/BIS). If it's a partnership/company, SC/ST owners must hold more than 51% share.
Documents Required: Udyam & GST registration copy, PAN card, Caste certificate, Partnership/company documents (if applicable), Test payment receipt & GST invoice, Lab test report (NABL/BIS stamped), Cancelled cheque of business bank account
How to Apply: Go to the National SC-ST Hub website, sign up with your name/email/phone, create a password, log in, fill in your details, and submit the form online.

Financial Benefit: You get an E-rickshaw shop with daily essential items (like rice, sugar, oil) to sell door-to-door. You can keep a profit of ₹2–3 per kg/litre you sell.
Target Location: Assam only (must be a permanent resident
Target Community / Category: Unemployed educated youth (no caste/community restriction)
Business Type / Industry: Mobile retail shop — selling daily essential household items door-to-door
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: (1) you are 18 or older, (2) you live in Assam, (3) you are unemployed, (4) you have passed HSLC (class 10) or an equivalent exam, (5) your name is registered at the Employment Exchange. Note: you must follow the officer's rules on schedule, pricing, and area, or your licence can be cancelled and you may have to return the aid with interest
Documents Required: Age proof; Address proof; ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Driving License); Education certificate; Experience certificate (if any); Photographs
How to Apply: Applications are invited by your local Deputy Commissioner/Sub-Divisional Officer/Principal Secretary office. Selection is based on your education, past experience, and financial condition — not a fixed online form

Scheme Name: Swahid Dayal Das Panika Swaniyojan Achoni
Financial Benefit: Money to help you start or grow your own self-employed work (exact amount not stated in text)
Target Location: Assam only (must be a permanent resident)
Target Community / Category: Tea Tribes and Adivasi community
Business Type / Industry: Any self-employment activity/trade
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if: (1) you are 20–35 years old, (2) you live in Assam and belong to the Tea Tribes or Adivasi community, (3) you are already self-employed, (4) your family owns less than 10 bighas of land, (5) you or your family has not received this benefit in the last 3 years, (6) only one person per family can apply. Note: you cannot apply if you work for the government, a Panchayat body, a selection committee, or as permanent staff at a tea garden. People with disabilities and those with 3 months of skills training get preference
Documents Required: Passport photo; Signature; Date of birth certificate; Age proof (birth certificate or school leaving certificate); Caste certificate; A signed note confirming you have less than 10 bighas of land; A signed note about your family's income; Voter ID/PAN/Driving License; Aadhaar card; A signed declaration with your photo standing in front of your business; A recommendation letter from the Chairman; First page of your bank passbook
How to Apply: Apply online through the SIRISH portal (via www.ttwd.assam.gov.in) — register or log in, select the scheme, fill in your personal and location details, upload your documents, add your bank details, review everything, and submit. You'll get an application number to track your status

Financial Benefit: ₹5,000 stall rent support inside Assam; ₹15,000 stall rent support outside Assam; daily allowance of ₹50 per stall within district, ₹600 outside district, and ₹500 outside Assam; 2nd-class railway fare for 2 people for travel outside Assam
Target Community / Category: Small traders, farmers and artisans; caste certificate if applicable
Business Type / Industry: Existing small industries, trading, farming and artisan businesses
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Applicant must be 18–50 years old. The industry must be in a rural area of Assam, already operating continuously for at least 2 years, and have its own workshed for production. No educational qualification is required.
Documents Required: Passport-size photograph; industry registration; caste certificate if applicable; training certificate if available; cancelled cheque with proprietor's name; quotation from fair organisation showing stall rent
How to Apply: Get/download the Biponi application form, fill it in the required format, attach the documents and submit it to the District Industries and Commerce Centre (DICC).

Financial Benefit: Funding up to 90% of project cost, with project cost up to ₹50 crore considered. Supports prototype development, trials and defence technology. Up to 20% support may be provided to incubators associated with nascent startups.
Target Community / Category: MSMEs, startups, public/private companies, partnership firms, LLPs, one-person companies and sole proprietorships registered in India
Business Type / Industry: Defence technology, defence manufacturing, prototypes, innovative products and processes
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Applicant must be an Indian-registered company, firm or business. Startups must be DPIIT-recognized. Nascent startups must be less than 3 years old and incubated at a Central/State government-assisted incubator. The startup must be at least 51% owned and controlled by a Resident Indian citizen and must not have received government funding for the same technology.
Documents Required: Detailed Project Update Report; Utilization Certificate and Statement of Expenses (UC & SE); Chartered Accountant Certificate for subsequent instalments; other application details/documents as required
How to Apply: Apply online on the TDF portal. Register with name, contact, organisation, registration type and focus area. Confirm Indian ownership with at least 51% resident Indian shareholding, accept terms, verify captcha and register. Then log in and submit the required details.

Financial Benefit: Startups/entrepreneurs can get up to ₹1 crore. Incubators can receive up to ₹10 crore in phases to support startups.
Target Community / Category: Entrepreneurs, startups, students, researchers and innovators with innovative ideas
Business Type / Industry: Technology, innovation and startup businesses
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Open to entrepreneurs, startups, students, researchers and innovators who have innovative ideas, technologies, products or services. Support for startups is provided through incubators.
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card or valid government ID; Startup Registration Certificate if applicable; Business Plan/Project Proposal; Pitch Deck; Incubation Certificate or recommendation letter from incubator
How to Apply: Apply online through the DST e-PMS Portal. Register as a new applicant, create a login, enter personal and organisation/startup details, submit the form and create the password using the confirmation email.

Financial Benefit: Up to ₹15 lakh per idea for developing and nurturing ideas. Up to ₹1 crore for plant, machinery, hardware and software for R&D and common facilities.
Target Community / Category: Technical colleges, universities, professional colleges/institutes, R&D institutes, eligible NGOs, MSME-DIs, Technology Centres and Central/State Government organisations
Business Type / Industry: Business incubation, R&D, technology and innovation support
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Eligible institutions can apply to become a Host Institute (HI) and Business Incubator (BI). The institution should support new ideas, innovation and technology development for MSMEs.
Documents Required: University affiliation; AICTE approval; NABL or other accreditation; last 2 years audited annual accounts with auditor's report; any other required documents
How to Apply: Apply online. Register as HI on the official portal, enter details and submit. After login, select "Apply for HI/BI Approval", fill the application and click "Final Submit".

Financial Benefit: Equity/equity-linked funding for startups through SEBI-registered AIFs. FFS has a ₹10,000 crore corpus. Supported AIFs must invest at least 2 times the FFS contribution in startups.
Minimum Age: Startup up to 10 years old from incorporation
Target Community / Category: DPIIT-recognized startups; funding is provided indirectly through eligible AIFs
Business Type / Industry: Startups working on innovation, technology, research, or improving products, processes, or services
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: FFS directly supports eligible Category I or II AIFs, not individual startups. AIFs must be registered with SEBI or have applied, have a corpus below ₹1,000 crore, invest in startups, and agree to invest at least twice the FFS contribution. Startups receiving investment must be DPIIT-recognized and up to 10 years old.
Documents Required: AIF registration certificate; IM Agreement; past track record if any; PPM; AIF and fund financials; Trust Deed; contributor details; Startup Certificate; KYC documents including Aadhaar, PAN, financials and CIBIL score
How to Apply: Apply online through the FFS process: eligibility check and registration, questionnaire, preliminary review, meetings, detailed application, due diligence, VCIC appraisal and presentation, SIDBI Executive Committee approval, Letter of Intent, agreement signing and onboarding. Startups should approach eligible AIFs.

Scheme Name: Loan Based Schemes For Safai Karamchari - Sanitary Marts Scheme
Financial Benefit: Loan up to 90% of project cost, maximum ₹15 lakh. Beneficiary contributes 10%. Interest up to 7% per year; 1% rebate for women and 0.50% rebate for timely repayment. Repayment up to 10 years.
Target Community / Category: Safai Karamcharis, waste pickers, identified manual scavengers and their dependents; registered Safai Karamchari cooperatives; associations/firms promoted by the target group
Business Type / Industry: Sanitary Mart / sanitation-related business
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Safai Karamcharis, waste pickers, identified manual scavengers and their dependents can apply. Registered cooperatives and legally formed groups/firms of the target group can also apply. A valid occupation/target-group certificate may be needed. A person already listed as a manual scavenger in the official government survey does not need another certificate. No income limit is fixed.
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card; Occupation Certificate; certificate from an approved local/government authority; any other required documents
How to Apply: Submit the loan application to the District Office of the State Channelizing Agency (SCA), or a branch of an RRB/Nationalised Bank. The application is checked and the viable project is sent to NSKFDC for approval. After approval and loan agreement, the money is released through the SCA/bank.

Financial Benefit: Helps MSEs get government/PSU tender orders; NSIC can help with EMD and security deposits; helps access credit and raw materials.
Target Community / Category: Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs); SC/ST-owned units get exemption from enlistment fee
Business Type / Industry: Manufacturing/service MSEs; not pure trading without value addition
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Must be a Micro or Small Enterprise registered with NSIC under SPRS, or apply for SPRS registration with required documents. The factory/unit must be inspected before tender participation. Businesses doing only trading without value addition, packing or branding are not eligible.
Documents Required: Passport-size photo and residential proof of Proprietor/Partner/Director/Society office bearers; self-attested G.P. Registration Certificate; Power of Attorney/Board Resolution/Society Resolution; bank-attested specimen signature; recent supply orders; enlistment fee
How to Apply: Fill the prescribed application form (Annexure A/A-1), sign it by the authorized person, attach all required documents, and submit it to the concerned/regional NSIC branch office.

Scheme Name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
Financial Benefit: Government gives 35% of your project cost back (up to ₹10 lakh) after you take a bank loan. Self-help group members can get ₹40,000 each for working money and small tools.
Target Gender: All genders (special support for women-led groups)
Target Community / Category: Individual owners, Self-Help Groups, Farmer Producer Organizations, cooperatives — special focus on women's groups
Business Type / Industry: Food-related businesses only — pickle-making, spices, bakery, millet products, oil, dairy, and similar food processing work
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must already run or want to start a small food-making business (like pickle, spice, or bakery work). Your unit must be unregistered/informal right now — this scheme helps you become official. You must arrange some money yourself; rest comes from bank loan + this subsidy.
Documents Required: Aadhaar card, voter ID or driving license or passport, 2 passport photos, address proof, project report, bank account details
How to Apply: Apply online at pmfme.mofpi.gov.in. Fill your business details, upload documents, and it goes to a bank for loan approval.

Financial Benefit: Toolkit money ₹15,000. Loan up to ₹3 lakh (₹1 lakh first part, ₹2 lakh second part) at 5% interest. ₹500 per day during training. ₹1 per digital payment, up to 100 payments a month
Target Location: All India (extra help for North East, island and hilly areas)
Target Community / Category: Artisan families; extra focus on SC, ST, OBC, disabled persons
Business Type / Industry: Carpenter, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, tailor, cobbler, boat maker, mason, sculptor, and other hand-craft trades
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be 18 or older. You must work with your hands making or fixing things. You must not have a government job in your family. Only one person per family can apply.
Documents Required: Aadhaar card, mobile number linked to Aadhaar, bank account details, passport photo, proof of your trade if you have it
How to Apply: Go to your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) and ask to register. It is free.

Financial Benefit: Business loan with no collateral needed. Four levels: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh), Tarun Plus (₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh, only for people who already repaid a Tarun loan). Interest rate depends on the bank, usually 9% to 12% per year.
Target Gender: All genders (extra support for women entrepreneurs)
Target Community / Category: Small business owners; nearly 2 out of 3 loans go to women
Business Type / Industry: Any small non-farm business — shop, trading, manufacturing, or services (also dairy, beekeeping, and similar farm-linked work)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be 18 to 65 years old. You must run a small business (not a company) that is not farming crops. You must not need to give any land, gold, or property as security.
Documents Required: ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/PAN), address proof, passport photo, business proof (registration or address of shop), bank statements (if asked), quotation for equipment (if buying machinery)
How to Apply: Apply online at the Udyamimitra or JanSamarth portal, or visit any bank branch (SBI, PNB, HDFC, and most banks/NBFCs offer this loan)

Financial Benefit: Government gives back 15% to 35% of your project cost as a gift (not to repay). Rest comes as a bank loan. Manufacturing: up to ₹50 lakh project. Service/business: up to ₹20 lakh project.
Target Community / Category: General category and Special category (SC, ST, OBC, Women, Ex-Servicemen, Disabled, North East, hill/border areas get more subsidy)
Business Type / Industry: Any new small manufacturing, service, or trading business (not farming)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You must be 18 or older. Your business must be brand new (not already running). If your project costs more than ₹10 lakh (manufacturing) or ₹5 lakh (service), you must have passed 8th standard in school. You put in only 5–10% of the money yourself; rest is loan + subsidy.
Documents Required: Aadhaar card, PAN card, passport photo, address proof, project report (what your business will do), 8th standard pass certificate (if needed), caste certificate (if applying under special category)
How to Apply: Apply online at kviconline.gov.in (PMEGP e-portal). Fill the form, upload documents and project report, then it goes to a bank for approval.

Financial Benefit: Grant up to ₹20 lakh for building and testing your idea. Grant up to ₹50 lakh (as loan-type support) to enter the market and sell. Money is given in parts as you hit goals, not all at once.
Target Community / Category: Any Indian founder; company must be majority Indian-owned (51%+)
Business Type / Industry: New, innovative businesses (tech, product, or service ideas — not a regular shop)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: Your company must be officially recognized as a "Startup" by the government (DPIIT). It must be less than 2 years old. It must have a new or unique idea, not a copy of existing business. You should not have already gotten more than ₹10 lakh in past government help.
Documents Required: DPIIT recognition certificate, company registration papers, PAN, founder ID proof, business plan/pitch deck, bank account details
How to Apply: Apply online at seedfund.startupindia.gov.in. Choose an incubator near you, submit your idea, and pitch it if shortlisted. Money comes through the incubator, not directly.

Scheme Name: PM SVANidhi (Prime Minister's Street Vendor's Atmanirbhar Nidhi)
Financial Benefit: Loan of ₹10,000 (1st time), ₹20,000 (2nd time), ₹50,000 (3rd time). Low interest. Extra cashback for using digital payment.
Target Community / Category: Any community, no restriction
Business Type / Industry: Street vending (selling on carts, footpaths, small stalls)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if you were selling on the street before 24 March 2020 and have a vending certificate or ID card from your local city office. Even without a certificate, you can apply if your name is on the city's street vendor list.
Documents Required: Vending Certificate or ID Card (if you don't have one, your name on the survey list works), Aadhaar Card, Bank Account
How to Apply: Apply online on the PM SVANidhi website, or visit your nearest bank, or go to a Common Service Centre (CSC) near you for help applying.

Financial Benefit: Government buys your handmade woven items directly from you, no middleman, so you get fair payment. Money is sent to your bank account.
Target Community / Category: Indigenous weaver families
Business Type / Industry: Handloom weaving (traditional hand-woven items)
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can join if you live in Assam, are a woman, have at least one handloom at home, and have a bank account. People from other states cannot apply. An officer will visit and check before you're approved.
Documents Required: Bank Account (with CBS), Proof you live in Assam, Proof you have a handloom at home
How to Apply: Go to the Swanirbhar Naari website (swanirbharnaari.assam.gov.in) and register with your details and documents. Wait for a government officer to visit and verify.

Financial Benefit: ₹2 lakh (general) or ₹5 lakh (professional degree holders) — half is free money (grant), half is a loan with no interest
Target Community / Category: Educated unemployed youth, no caste/community restriction
Business Type / Industry: Any small business or self-employment venture
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if you live in Assam, are between 28-45 years old, have finished at least higher secondary school, are jobless, and have not taken this scheme before (only one person per family can apply).
Documents Required: Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport/Driving License, Bank Passbook (first page), Employment Exchange registration
How to Apply: Register online on the CMAAA portal, wait for the application window to open, then log in again to submit your business plan and documents.

Financial Benefit: Loan up to ₹10 lakh. Government pays 5% of the bank's interest for you, so your loan is cheaper. No fees to pay for paperwork.
Target Community / Category: Any community, no restriction
Business Type / Industry: New startups, new small businesses (MSME), any innovative business idea
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if you are starting a new business or MSME in Assam and have not failed to repay a bank loan before. People who already did skill training get priority.
Documents Required: Application form (Form-A), 2 passport photos, ID proof, business plan/project report
How to Apply: Apply through Assam Gramin Vikas Bank (AGVB) or your local DIC (District Industries Centre) office with the application form and documents.

Financial Benefit: ₹10,000 free money in year 1. ₹25,000 more in year 2 (half free, half small loan). Up to ₹50,000 more in year 3 if you use the money well. Total ₹35,000-₹85,000.
Target Community / Category: General/OBC women: max 3 children. SC/ST/Tea Tribe women: max 4 children
Business Type / Industry: Small business, shop, food, handicraft, weaving, or any small trade
Plain-Text Eligibility Summary: You can apply if you are a woman in a Self Help Group (SHG) in Assam, and your number of children is within the limit for your community. If your daughter is school-age, she must be going to school.
Documents Required: SHG Membership proof, Business Plan, Bank Account, ID proof
How to Apply: Get the form from your Gaon Panchayat office, fill it and submit it there. Your SHG will help you with the process.
